title: pass@k, entropy collapse, and RLVR on a toy arithmetic task
brief: Build the unbiased pass@k estimator, a verifiable answer reward, and the entropy covariance law, then train a toy arithmetic model with RLVR and watch pass@1 rise while pass@64 falls. The GPU run trains Qwen3-0.6B-Base R1-Zero style.
hints: C(n - c, k) / C(n, k) equals the product over j from n - c + 1 to n of (1 - k / j). np.prod(1 - k / np.arange(n - c + 1, n + 1)) computes it. When n - c < k, every size-k subset holds a correct sample, so pass@k is 1.
In answer_reward, re.search(r'</think>\s*<answer>(.*?)</answer>', text, re.DOTALL) finds the first answer block after the thinking. Then re.fullmatch(r'-?\d+', content.strip()) accepts integers only.

zero_signal_probability: a group has all-equal rewards when every sample is right (probability p ** G) or every sample is wrong ((1 - p) ** G). Add both, and use np.asarray(p) so an array of pass rates works.
pg_loss: zero the padding with torch.where before multiplying, since -inf times 0 is nan. Divide by mask.sum(), the total token count, not by the batch size.
token_entropy: p * log p is nan where the logit is -inf. torch.where(p > 0, p * logp, 0) fixes it.
entropy_change_estimate: center both log pi and delta_logits by their means under pi, multiply, weight by pi, sum over the last axis, and negate.

In train_rlvr_toy, the batch is torch.arange(16).repeat_interleave(group_size), so each question's group is contiguous. Get per-token log-probs with torch.log_softmax(model.logits(problems, tokens), -1).gather(-1, tokens[..., None]).squeeze(-1).
